body: Flag: CLEAN (HCL Tech) with a legacy blemish (HCL Infosystems). HCL Technologies (promoter ~60%) has been a high-payout company: quarterly dividends with a stated ~75%+ payout policy and occasional buybacks; no promoter pledging; no SEBI findings against promoters. Succession was handled in steps: Roshni Nadar Malhotra became chair of HCL Tech (2020), and by gift deeds of 6-Mar-2025 Shiv Nadar gave her 47% of promoter vehicles Vama Sundari Investments (Delhi) and HCL Corp (his stake 51% -> 4%; hers 10.33% -> ~57.3%), giving her voting control of ~44.3% of HCL Tech; SEBI exempted the open offer and total promoter holding stayed ~60.8%. Legacy blemish: HCL Infosystems (hardware/distribution) shrank into heavy losses through the 2010s, eroding its minority shareholders' value; it was eventually wound into the group (details unverified). HCL Tech's large IBM software IP purchase (2019, $1.8bn) was a capital-allocation debate, not a governance breach. Investor read: one of the cleaner promoter-led IT names; the payout policy is the key minority protection.

data.status_2026: Roshni Nadar controlling promoter since Mar-2025
